## Setup

### Packages

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Packages to use
# tidyverse includes ggplot2
# janitor and DataExplorer are good for data wrangling 
packages = c("tidyverse", "janitor", "DataExplorer")


packageCheck = function(x) {
    if (!require(x, character.only = TRUE)) {
      install.packages(x, dependencies = TRUE)
      library(x, character.only = TRUE)
    }
  }

## Now load or install & load all
loadPacks<-lapply(packages, packageCheck)
```

## Data Wrangling 
### Clean covariate data
Covariate data includes metadata in values spaces that needs to be removed. Some column names can be shortened for clarity and concision. 

```{r}
cleanCovar <- covar %>%
  separate(col="mat_age_yrs", into = c(NA, "mat_age"), sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="preg_preeclampsia", into = c(NA, "preg_preeclampsia"), sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="delivery_gestAge_wks", into = c(NA, "delivery_weeks"), sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="sampleCollection_gestAge_wks", into = c(NA, "sample_weeks"), sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="batch_Microarray", into = c(NA, "batch_Microarray"), sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="mat_BMI", into = c(NA, "mat_BMI"), sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="mat_vitD", into = c(NA, "mat_vitD"), sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="mat_asthma", into = c(NA, "mat_asthma"), sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE)
```

### Add gene names to gene expression data
```{r}
named_genes <- geneExp %>%
  rename(PROBEID = X) %>%
  left_join(geneNames, by = "PROBEID")
```

### Pivot named genes into a long data frame
```{r}
long_genes <- named_genes %>%
  pivot_longer(col = c(starts_with("GSM")), values_to = "geneExp", names_to = "geoID")
```

### Join covariate data and gene expression data
```{r}
long_cov_genes <- long_genes %>%
  left_join(cleanCovar, by = "geoID")
```

### Turn two categorical covariates into factors
```{r}
# Preeclampsia status
long_cov_genes$preg_preeclampsia <- factor(long_cov_genes$preg_preeclampsia)

# Maternal asthma status
long_cov_genes$mat_asthma <- factor(ifelse(long_cov_genes$mat_asthma == 1, "Asthma", "Not Asthma"))
```

### Turn on continuous covariate into a categorical covariate
```{r}
# Delivery weeks in buckets
# Very Early: before 36 weeks
# Early: between 36 and 38 weeks
# On time: between 38 and 40 weeks
# Late: after 40 weeks
long_cov_genes$delivery_time <- factor(ifelse(long_cov_genes$delivery_weeks < 36, "Very Early", ifelse(long_cov_genes$delivery_weeks < 38, "Early", ifelse(long_cov_genes$delivery_weeks > 40, "Late", "On Time"))), levels = c("Very Early (Before 36 weeks)", "Early (Before 38 weeks)", "On Time (Between 38 and 40 weeks)", "Late (After 40 weeks)"), ordered = TRUE)
levels(long_cov_genes$delivery_time)
```

## Submission 1: Gene of interest: RASAL3
RASAL3 plays a role in signalling and T cell regulation. It is associated with diverticulitis and epiphyseal dysplasia. 

Feedback from submission 1: make sure that plots can stand alone. Include information about definitions of pregnancy status in legends, axes, etc. 


### Subset data containing all genes to only look at RASAL3
```{r}
RASAL3_exp <- long_cov_genes[which(long_cov_genes$GENE == "RASAL3"),]
```

### Plot 1: Histogram of gene expression
```{r}
ggplot(RASAL3_exp, aes(x = geneExp)) +
  geom_histogram() + 
  labs(x = "Gene Expression of RASAL3",
       y = "Frequency",
       title = "RASAL3 Gene Expression in Subset of VDAART Study"
       ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### Plot 2: Scatterplot of covariate versus gene expression 
```{r}
ggplot(RASAL3_exp, aes(x = mat_vitD, y = geneExp)) +
  geom_point() + 
  labs(
    title = "Maternal Vitamin D vs. Gene Expression of RASAL3 at Trial Entry (10-18 Weeks Gestation)",
    x = "Maternal Vitamin D (ng/mL)",
    y = "Expression of RASAL3") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = 'y ~ x') +
  theme_bw()
```

### Plot 3: Boxplot of gene expression separated by both categorical variables
```{r}
# Need to reorder factor levels of delivery_time first
#RASAL3_exp$delivery_time = with(RASAL3_exp, reorder())
# Plot
ggplot(RASAL3_exp, aes(x = delivery_time, y = geneExp, color = preg_preeclampsia)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Gene Expression of RASAL3 with Pregnancy Duration and Preeclampsia Status",
    x = "Pregnancy Duration",
    y = "Expression of RASAL3",
    color = "Preeclampsia Status"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```


## Submission 2: Define function to produce plots

### Histogram Function
```{r}
# Histogram
create_histogram <- function(df, geneName){
  # x is gene expression 
  ggplot(df, aes(x = geneExp)) +
    geom_histogram() + 
    labs(
      title = "__ Gene Expression in Subset of VDAART Study",
      x = "Gene Expression of __",
      y = "Frequency" # find units 
    ) +
    theme_bw()
}
```

### Scatterplot Function
```{r}
create_scatterplot <- function(df, geneName, contCov){
  # x is covariate, y is gene expression
  ggplot(df, aes(x = contCov)) + 
    geom_point() +
    labs(
      title = "Maternal Vitamin D vs. Gene Expression of ___ at Trial Entry (10-18 Weeks Gestation)",
      x = "Maternal Vitamin D (ng/mL)", # contCov
      y = "Expression of Gene" # geneName 
    ) +
    theme_bw()
}
```

### Boxplot Function
```{r}
create_boxplot <- function(df, geneName, catCov1, catCov2){
  # x is gene exp, y is first categorical variable, color is second categorical variable
  # if using pregnancy duration like as default, remember to further define 
  #x_1 <- df[catCov1]
  # get the column from the dataframe where the column name matches the input text 
  boxplot <- ggplot(df, aes(x = x_1, y = geneExp, color = catCov2)) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    labs(
      x = geneName,
      y = catCov1,
      color = catCov2
    ) +
    theme_bw()
  return(boxplot)
}
```

## Define function to create all three plots for a given gene 
```{r}
create_plot <- function(df, geneName, contCov, catCov1, catCov2){
  # get only the actually relevant parts of the dataframe 
  cat(geneName)
  head(df)
  (gene <- df[which(df$GENE == geneName),])
  
  # technically would not have to pass in geneName now since only the one gene 
  # but this way don't have to get it again, might have formatting issues or something
  create_histogram(gene, geneName)
  create_scatterplot(gene, geneName, contCov)
  return(create_boxplot(gene, geneName, catCov1, catCov2))
}
```

## Define function to iterate over list of genes 
```{r}
# function to create all of three plots for each gene name given
# it's not going to like the defaults here, probably need to change to strings but then might need to change back
create_plots <- function(df, geneNames, contCov = "mat_vitD", catCov1 = "delivery_time", catCov2 = "preg_preeclampsia"){
  head(df)
  dim(df)
  for (i in geneNames) {
    cat(i)
    return(create_plot(df, i, contCov, catCov1, catCov2))
    
    # save in group of plots
  }
  return(dim(df))
}
```

## Call function to produce plots
```{r}
geneNames = c("RASAL3", "UNC13A", "IL13")
#head(long_cov_genes)
allPlots <- create_plots(df = long_cov_genes, geneNames = geneNames, contCov = "mat_vitD", catCov1 = "delivery_time", catCov2 = "preg_preeclampsia")
allPlots
```
